content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint may not capture dose-response relationship",
      "quote": "The primary objective of the study is to assess the efficacy of REGN3500 monotherapy in AD, as well as understand the dose-response relationship, compared with placebo treatment",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "2.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary objective includes understanding the dose-response relationship, but the primary endpoint is only percent change in EASI at week 16, which may not be sufficient to characterize dose-response across multiple doses. The protocol does not specify a dose-response analysis or a model-based endpoint.",
      "fix": "Consider adding a dose-response analysis as a key secondary or exploratory endpoint, or specify a dose-response model in the SAP."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for inadequate response to topical medication is ambiguous",
      "quote": "Documented recent history (within 6 months before the screening visit) of inadequate response to topical AD medication(s) or for whom topical treatments are medically inadvisable",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The definition of inadequate response is complex and may be interpreted variably. The note allows for a trial of TCS during screening, but the criteria for 'inadequate response' during that trial are not clearly defined (e.g., what level of improvement is required). This could lead to enrollment of patients who are not truly inadequate responders, or to amendments to clarify.",
      "fix": "Specify a quantitative threshold for inadequate response (e.g., less than 50% improvement in EASI) during the screening treatment trial."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for TB testing is incomplete",
      "quote": "Patients with a positive TB QuantiFERON test result at screening will be excluded from the study.",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "6.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol excludes patients with positive QuantiFERON but does not specify how indeterminate results are handled, nor does it require evaluation for latent TB (e.g., chest X-ray) for patients with positive results. This is a safety gap for an immunomodulatory biologic.",
      "fix": "Add a note on handling indeterminate QuantiFERON results and require a chest X-ray or other evaluation for latent TB before exclusion."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring for liver function is missing",
      "quote": "Severe concomitant illness(es) that, in the investigator’s judgment, would adversely affect the patient’s participation in the study. Examples include, but are not limited to, ... hepatobiliary conditions (eg, Child-Pugh class B or C)",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "6.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol excludes patients with severe hepatobiliary conditions but does not specify routine monitoring of liver function tests (LFTs) during the study. Given that REGN3500 is a monoclonal antibody, liver enzyme elevations are a potential safety concern. The Schedule of Activities likely includes LFTs, but the text does not mention a stopping rule or specific monitoring frequency for LFTs.",
      "fix": "Add a section on liver safety monitoring, including periodic LFT assessments and criteria for dose interruption or discontinuation in case of significant elevations."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for pruritus NRS may be burdensome",
      "quote": "A minimum of 4 daily scores out of the 7 days is required to calculate the baseline average score. For patients who do not have at least 4 daily scores reported during the 7 days immediately preceding the planned randomization date, randomization should be postponed until this requirement is met, but without exceeding the 35-day maximum duration for screening.",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring at least 4 daily scores in the 7 days before randomization may be difficult for some patients, leading to delays or exclusions. This could increase screening failure rates and burden on patients.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing a lower minimum (e.g., 3 days) or a longer assessment window, or provide a backup method for assessing baseline pruritus."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for live vaccines is overly broad",
      "quote": "Treatment with a live (attenuated) vaccine within 12 weeks before the baseline visit",
      "page": 32,
      "section": "6.2.2",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 12-week washout for live vaccines is longer than typical (often 4-6 weeks) and may unnecessarily exclude patients. This could lead to amendments or recruitment challenges.",
      "fix": "Shorten the washout to 4 weeks or align with standard guidelines for immunosuppressive biologics."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoint for pruritus onset is not well-defined",
      "quote": "Time to onset of effect on pruritus during the 16-week treatment period (≥4-point reduction of weekly average of daily peak Pruritus NRS from baseline)",
      "page": 27,
      "section": "4.2.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The endpoint 'time to onset' is ambiguous: it does not specify whether the reduction must be sustained for a certain duration or if it is the first occurrence. This could lead to different interpretations in analysis.",
      "fix": "Define 'onset' as the first week where the reduction is achieved and sustained for at least two consecutive weeks, or specify in the SAP."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring for immunogenicity is not detailed",
      "quote": "To assess the immunogenicity of REGN3500 in adult patients with moderate-to-severe AD",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The secondary objective includes immunogenicity, but the protocol does not specify how anti-drug antibodies (ADA) will be monitored, including timing of samples and impact on safety or efficacy. This is a gap for a biologic.",
      "fix": "Add a subsection on immunogenicity assessments, including ADA sampling schedule and analysis plan."
    }
  ]
}
